Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — baseline throughput and SLA fit

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to scope a 6-week POC on dedicated capacity for our clinical summarization workflow (internal model: open-encoder-8B). Before we pull procurement in, can you confirm:

- A reasonable tokens/sec estimate for our expected mix (avg input length ~1.2k tokens, generation avg 300 tokens).
- Whether a 99th percentile latency SLO of 400ms for single-request interactive calls is feasible with a dedicated slab (we expect 120 concurrent active users at peak).
- The safety margin / headroom you typically recommend for a POC vs production commit.

If you can send a short runbook + numbers we can attach to our internal business case that'd be great.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Price
Director, AI Platforms | Cascade Health

--

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — baseline throughput and SLA fit

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask, and happy to jump in. High level up-front: yes, a dedicated slab can meet a 400ms p99 in many configurations, but it depends on model config, quantization, burst concurrency, and whether you need streaming.

I'll attach a concise throughput model (spreadsheet) — it contains tokens/sec estimates across three config tiers (quantized int8, bf16, mixed). Quick highlights here:

- Baseline (single 80GB A100-like GPU equiv) for open-encoder-8B at q8_perf: ~55--70 tokens/sec for generation-only at median; p99 latencies vary (700ms+ without batching).
- Recommended POC slab: 4x 80GB-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache for prompt prefixing => estimated steady tokens/sec aggregate 900--1,100 t/s, supporting burst headroom to ~1,500 t/s.
- For your 120 concurrent active users (assume 1.2 requests/minute/user at peak), expected steady concurrency ~2.4 RPS; with average output 300 tokens this maps to ~720 t/s steady — fits middle of recommended slab with ~25% headroom.

Ask: Marcus, can you verify the p99 numbers with the latency model and add notes on queuing under burst?

Jordan — I'll schedule a short call tomorrow to walk the numbers. Monica, looping you for procurement timeline and contract hooks if this POC looks good.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — baseline throughput and SLA fit

Hey all — ran the numbers in the attached spreadsheet (see tab 'LatencySim'). Key technical notes and assumptions:

- Model assumptions: avg prompt prefix length 1,200 tokens, generation 300 tokens, seq_length peaks at 2k tokens for a subset (5% traffic). We simulated both streaming (chunked generation) and non-streaming.
- Kernel/quantization: q8_perf (mixed int8 kernels) gives best t/s to latency tradeoff for this architecture; q4 impacts latency unpredictably for long context.

Latency simulation summary (p99):
- 1x80GB equiv (no batching): p99 ~980ms (non-streaming), ~850ms (streaming chunked)
- 4x80GB equiv w/ continuous batching (our POC config): p99 ~320--420ms depending on batch sizing and request concurrency distribution
- Autoscaling/burst buffer (additional 2 GPUs warm standby): reduces p99 to ~280--350ms under 2x burst.

Headroom guidance: for a POC we recommend nominal headroom target 20--30% above expected steady tokens/sec. For production commits we size for 2.5x peak expected to handle unanticipated traffic patterns and protect SLOs.

Operational notes:
- Enable prefix KV caching for common system prompts to reduce compute for repeated contexts.
- Configure request-level throttles with graceful 429 -> fallback path to smaller model for heavy bursts.

Jordan — happy to present the sim during the call and walk sensitivity to sequence-length tails.

Marcus Lin
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — quick wrap after internal sync with Marcus and Monica:

- Short answer: POC configuration (4x80GB-equivalent + 2 warm standby) should meet the 400ms p99 in the common-case and provide ~25--40% headroom for your expected steady traffic.
- If you have a 5% tail of long sequences (~2k tokens) we see p99 drift upward; two mitigations: 1) cap max generation length per request for interactive flows; 2) route long-batch offline tasks to a background pipeline.

Next steps:
- Jordan to confirm PO / procurement preference (PO vs CC) and whether Cascade wants our standard MSA or to send redlines by EOD Mon 4/26.
- Priya/Marcus: schedule 45-min call to walk sim and show latency variance (I'll send calendar invite).
